incident-bot: [2001-11-22T09:12:14Z] Pager: SEV2 - routing fallback observed on /v1/generate — paging oncall@eng-oncall. Symptoms: elevated 503s, increased tail latency >5s for some p95, partial customer impact. Auto-remediation attempted: fallback to model-variant 'gpt-small-ff' succeeded for 40% of requests. See runbook: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/routing-fallback :pager:
Maya G: I'm on it. grabbing the initial metrics now. Anybody seeing traffic spikes from a single customer? pinging @ops-bot for infra metrics.
Liam H: I saw a spike in QPS from svc-analytics at 09:09 UTC, but not sure if correlated.
Anika R: oncall here. I'm taking lead for live mitigation. Maya — can you grab the last 15m of LB logs and error rates? I'll triage model pool health.
Maya G: pulling logs now. quick snippet:
```
[09:06:21] svc-analytics -> 1200 req/s
[09:07:02] 502/503 rising on node gpu-05
[09:08:50] routing fallback triggered to gpt-small-ff
```
Maya G: looks like 503s started at ~09:07. spikes from svc-analytics definitely correlate.
Samir P: adding context — we had a recent canary for autoscaler config (scale-down quicker). wondering if aggressive scale-down reduced capacity.
ops-bot: infra-metrics: GPU pool utilization for seqlen<=512: gpu-05=99%, gpu-03=96%, autoscaler activity: last scale-up 09:02, last scale-down 09:05.
Anika R: thanks. mitigation plan: 1) revert aggressive scale-down for that pool, 2) temporarily increase burst capacity, 3) monitor fallback rate. I will open a quick PR to bump min-replicas.
Liam H: +1. Also enabling request-sampling to capture failing prompts for postmortem analysis (sensitive data scrubbed).
Maya G: customer-impact hypothesis: svc-analytics had a poorly batched bulk request pattern causing hotspot on a small subset of shards. Some customer requests returned degraded quality via fallback but not full data loss. I'll contact CSM if impact confirmed.
Product Lead: If this affected an enterprise contract, we should notify CS and legal. Maya, could you confirm percentage of impacted requests?
Maya G: preliminary: ~2.3% of total generated tokens in the region routed to fallback for ~4m window. Some high-value requests experienced latency >10s.
Anika R: live actions executed: reverted autoscaler commit 5f3a2, increased min-replicas from 8->12 for dedicated-route-3, bumped burst pool to +4 GPUs. Fallback rate dropped to 0.6% after 09:12.
Samir P: rolling logs show error causes: KV cache overflow on gpu-05 leading to eviction storms. Possibly exacerbated by long-context requests from svc-analytics.
Maya G: contacting svc-analytics eng lead (cc @Liam H). Liam, can you loop them in and ask for their request pattern? Also create a short customer-impact note for CS.
Liam H: done. pinged @raj.svcanalytics in thread, asked for repro and whether they used unbounded batching.
raj.svcanalytics (external): replied — we ran a late-night analytics job that fan-out'd thousands of short prompts without batching. sorry, didn't expect that traffic.
Maya G: thanks, noted. Root cause working theory: traffic pattern + aggressive autoscaler + KV cache behaviour created hotspot and 503s. Immediate mitigations held.
incident-bot: [2001-11-22T09:20:40Z] Incident severity updated: SEV2 -> Monitoring. Postmortem scheduled. Use /postmortem create 2001122334.
Anika R: scheduling postmortem: proposing tomorrow 15:00 UTC to accommodate APAC. Who can lead the write-up?
Samir P: I can co-author the technical section (KV cache, autoscaler timeline). Maya can do customer impact summary. Product Lead can provide business context.
Kate L: I can facilitate the blameless section and run the retro. 15:00 UTC works for me.
Maya G: action items list to track in the postmortem:
- AI1: add autoscaler safety caps for dedicated-route-3 (owner: Anika)
- AI2: implement rate-limiter advisory for large fan-out jobs and public docs update (owner: Liam)
- AI3: add KV cache telemetry for eviction storms and alerts (owner: Samir)
- AI4: customer comms draft and CS notification (owner: Maya)
- AI5: brown-bag / training session to walk teams through prevention patterns (owner: Kate)
Samir P: estimated timelines: AI1 (2 days), AI2 (3 days), AI3 (1 week), AI4 (24 hours), AI5 (2 weeks).
Anika R: I'll open tasks in JIRA under INC-2001122334 and link them from the postmortem doc. Please tag each ticket with priority P1/P2.
Maya G: created draft postmortem at https://redwood.internal/postmortems/INC-2001122334 — adding timeline and logs. feel free to edit.
ops-bot: created ticket INC-2001122334-1 (autoscaler-safety) assigned to Anika R. due: 2d.
Liam H: for the brown-bag, suggest format: 30m technical walk-through + 15m Q&A, include slides on batching patterns, autoscaler caveats, KV cache mechanics.
Kate L: I'll schedule the brown-bag for 2020-11-24 16:00 UTC (2 weeks) and reserve 30m for playbook rehearsal. Calendar invite to go out after postmortem.
Product Lead: please include customer-facing remediation steps in the postmortem so CS can answer questions without delay.
Maya G: drafting customer note now. short version: "We observed transient degraded quality and latency for a subset of requests due to a traffic pattern causing resource contention. Mitigations deployed; no data loss. Next steps: autoscaler limits and improved telemetry." will share in doc.
Samir P: technical note: we'll also add a telemetry alert when KV eviction rate > 100/sec for 1m. That should preempt future storms.
Anika R: postmortem owners — please ensure action items are assigned before the meeting. We'll aim to close P1s within 2 weeks.
Maya G: quick retrospective takeaway for the brown-bag: "edge-case traffic patterns can create localized resource storms; throttles, autoscaler smoothing, and cache telemetry are our main defenses." Will capture slides.
Liam H: small follow-up — can the SDK docs include recommended batching patterns? I'll draft and PR to docs.
Kate L: added meeting agenda to postmortem doc: timeline, root cause analysis, action items, owner commitments, customer comms, brown-bag plan.
Maya G: thanks team. I'll post final incident summary to #general after postmortem for org visibility.
incident-bot: [2001-11-22T09:23:30Z] Incident closed to Monitoring state. Postmortem link: https://redwood.internal/postmortems/INC-2001122334 — meeting scheduled 2020-11-24 16:00 UTC.
Liam H: thanks everyone. good job moving fast and keeping customer impact minimal. :thumbsup:
Kate L: keeping this thread for postmortem edits. will ping again with invite. :calendar:
Maya G: closing oncall handoff — Anika, I'll hand you the doc and related logs. leaving notes in the doc about sensitive samples.
Anika R: received. I'll review before the meeting and prep the technical timeline.
ops-bot: log-export: /exports/INC-2001122334/logs.tar.gz (expires in 7d)
Maya G: noted. if no objections, I'll send CS the short customer note in 1h.
Product Lead: approve. thanks for the speedy mitigation and the clear next steps.
